Introduction

Can you earn high real estate returns without owning or managing properties? Yes, you can. At Macon County, Illinois’ annual Tax Lien Sale, you can bid on tax certificates and secure up to a 9% return paid out every six months! Macon County’s rich history and cultural landmarks make it an attractive prospect for investors.

Understanding Tax Lien Certificates

What are Tax Lien Certificates?

Tax lien certificates are financial instruments that allow investors to purchase delinquent property taxes. When property owners fail to pay their taxes, the county places a lien on the property and sells these liens at an auction.

How They Work

Investors bid on the interest rate they will accept. The process starts at a 9% interest rate, and the bid goes downward. The lowest bid wins. Property owners then have a redemption period, usually between 2.5 to 3 years, to pay back the taxes plus interest. If the owner fails to redeem the property, the lien holder can foreclose on the property.

Potential Returns

The interest rate on these tax liens can be up to 9%, applied every six months, adding a significant amount to the redemption cost. This makes tax lien certificates a lucrative investment option.

Steps to Start Tax Lien Investing

Research and Understand Local Laws

It’s crucial to know the legal framework in your target area. Check the local regulations and ensure you understand the procedures and risks involved.

Visit the Local Treasurer’s Website

For detailed tax sale information, visit the:

  • Macon County Treasurer’s Office
  • Property Tax Information

Check the Auction Site

Keep an eye on auction dates and available properties. The county’s website provides essential information about upcoming tax sales.

Read the Details about Tax Liens

Understand the sale schedule, parcel inquiry, and other essential details. Knowledge of these elements helps in making informed investment decisions.

Contact the County Office

For additional inquiries, contact the Macon County Treasurer’s Office at (217) 424-1426.

Pro Tips

  • Start Small: Begin with a few liens to understand the process.
  • Research Thoroughly: Ensure the properties are worth the investment.
  • Stay Updated: Keep track of redemption periods and interest payments.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

Popular Attractions

Macon County is known for its cultural landmarks and historical sites. Decatur, the county seat, offers parks, theaters, and museums for entertainment and education.

Transportation Infrastructure

The county boasts a robust transportation network, including major highways, railroads, and the Decatur Airport, ensuring easy access and connectivity.

Economic Development

Key sectors include agriculture, manufacturing, and technology. The county’s diverse economy supports sustainable growth and investment opportunities.

Community Appeal

Outdoor activities, eco-tourism, and community events make Macon County a vibrant place to live and invest in

FAQs for Tax Liens

Q: What happens if the property owner doesn’t redeem the lien?

A: If the owner fails to pay the taxes plus interest within the redemption period, you can foreclose on the property.

Q: How do I participate in the tax lien auction?

A: Visit the Macon County Treasurer’s website for auction dates and registration details.

Q: Can I inspect the properties before bidding?

A: It’s advisable to research and, if possible, inspect the properties beforehand.
